content: He who has gained freedom by the faculty of reason may go where he wills and say: 'No one has power over me; I have been set free by God.'
author: Epictetus
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. From childhood, we are trained to fit in, to smooth over our eccentricities, and to mirror the expectations of those around us. But copying others only buys superficial acceptance at the cost of your own soul.

Across his life and work, Epictetus saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Your unique perspective and lived contradictions are your greatest offering to the world. The moment you stop performing and stand firmly in your own skin, you command an authority that imitation can never manufacture.
reflectionPrompt: How can you integrate the essence of this wisdom into one specific decision or encounter today?
